white.$description: Used for icons on dark or colored backgrounds. Commonly applied in buttons or navigation.

light.$description: Used for disabled icons or low-emphasis actions.

lightDark.$description: Used for medium-emphasis icons across UI elements.

dark.$description: Used for primary interactive icons or leading visual elements.

success.$description: Used for icons representing positive status, success, or confirmation.

secondary.$description: Used for secondary status indicators, tags, or labels.

error.$description: Used for error, delete, or warning-related icons.

info.$description: Used for informational or guidance-related icons.

warning.$description: Used for icons representing warnings, alerts, or cautionary messages.

white.$description: Used for high-emphasis text on dark backgrounds or elevated surfaces. Ideal for titles, headings, or primary callouts.

light.$description: Used for secondary or supportive text, such as captions, sub-labels, or helper text.

lightDark.$description: Used for mid-level emphasis text. Suitable for subheadings, body content, or UI instructions.

dark.$description: Used for primary body text or content requiring strong readability. Recommended for paragraphs or main labels.

500.$description: Used for success messages, validation states, or confirmation labels.

600.$description: Used for emphasized success states such as headings or bold badges.

500.$description: Used for neutral or secondary messages, tags, or helper states.

600.$description: Used for emphasized secondary messages or muted status highlights.

500.$description: Used for error messages, warnings, invalid states, or critical alerts.

600.$description: Used for strong error emphasis in titles or alert components.

500.$description: Used for general information, tooltips, or onboarding content.

600.$description: Used for emphasized info highlights or headings.

500.$description: Used for warning messages, caution text, or status labels that require user attention.

600.$description: Used for emphasized warning states, such as headings or persistent alert messages.

white.$description: Base background used in default or blank surfaces. Commonly applied in cards, sheets, or canvas.

light.$description: Light surface backgrounds, often used for elevated containers or soft sections.

lightDark.$description: Neutral background with moderate contrast, suitable for dashboards or body surfaces.

dark.$description: Used for footer, sidebar, or overlays where high contrast foreground elements are required.

100.$description: Soft background for success messages, alerts, or banners.

500.$description: Primary success tone for containers, status blocks, or feedback sections.

600.$description: Stronger success background used for prominent notifications or modals.

100.$description: Light variant for secondary sections such as tags or labels.

500.$description: Main secondary color for content blocks, alerts, or accent containers.

600.$description: High-emphasis version for callouts or status-based components.

100.$description: Light background for error notifications or validation messages.

500.$description: Primary error tone used in alert blocks or danger zone components.

600.$description: High-emphasis background for critical error states or confirmations.

100.$description: Light info background used for tooltips, messages, or guidance blocks.

500.$description: Main info color for containers or status cards.

600.$description: Strong info tone used for high-contrast messaging or banners.

100.$description: Subtle warning background for alerts or notices.

500.$description: Main warning tone used for warning banners or critical guidance.

600.$description: Bold background for persistent warnings or high-visibility notices.

200.$description: Base neutral background for subdued containers or form inputs.

300.$description: Slightly darker neutral surface for sections, dividers, or UI panels.

400.$description: Strong neutral background used for toolbars, menus, or elevated containers.

white.$description: Used for outlines or dividers on dark backgrounds. Suitable for elevated elements and containers.

light.$description: Light stroke color for low-emphasis borders or separators. Often used in cards or grouped UI elements.

lightDark.$description: Medium-contrast stroke for general purpose outlines and surface boundaries.

dark.$description: High-emphasis stroke color for clear separation between UI sections or containers.

secondary.$description: Default stroke for secondary buttons or outlined button variants. Provides visual separation from backgrounds.

500.$description: Used for success-themed component borders, such as input validation or success states.

600.$description: Emphasized stroke for success indicators, progress borders, or badges.

500.$description: Secondary tone border used in tags, cards, or passive components.

600.$description: Stronger secondary stroke for higher visual prominence in UI boundaries.

500.$description: Error stroke for invalid input borders, warning outlines, or alert components.

600.$description: High-emphasis error border for critical error states or modal outlines.

500.$description: Used for borders or outlines related to informational content, such as tooltips or guidance boxes.

600.$description: Emphasized info border for callouts, highlighted tooltips, or info modals.

500.$description: Used for warning messages, status indicators, or bordered alert boxes.

600.$description: Strong warning border used to emphasize critical alerts or caution states.
